clauses.label: sole paragraph
clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 206 of the 
Labor Management Relations Act, 1947, 61 Stat. 155 (29 U.S.C. 176), 
I  hereby amend the first paragraph of Executive Order No. 11025 of 
June 7, 1962, entitled “Creating a Board of Inquiry to Report on a 
Labor Dispute Affecting the Aircraft Industry of the United States,” 
to read as follows:
.  “WHEREAS, there exists a labor dispute between Republic Avia­
tion Corporation, Farmingdale, Long Island, New York, and certain 
of its employees represented by Republic Lodge 1987, International 
Association of Machinists, A FL-CIO ; Local Union 775, United As­
sociation of Journeymen and Apprentices of the Plumbing and Pipe 
Fitting Industry of the United States and Canada, A FL -C IO ; In ­
ternational Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, Local Union 25, 
A FL-CIO ; Local Union 1318, United Brotherhood of Carpenters 
and Joiners of America, A FL-CIO ; and International Union of 
Operating Engineers, Local Unions 30 and 30-A, A FL -C IO ; and 
between John G. Sharp, Cafeteria Concessionaire at this Republic 
Aviation Corporation facility and certain employees represented by 
Local 164, Hotel and Restaurant Employees and Bartenders Inter­
national Union, A FL -C IO ; and”

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 5531) prints Executive Order 11026 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-06-08; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Amendment of Executive Order No. 11025, creating a Board of Inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the aircraft industry of the United States). I read the whole clause and signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers every operative sentence; I confirm it as complete. The one operative clause amends the first paragraph of Executive Order No. 11025 of June 7, 1962 (the Board of Inquiry on the aircraft-industry dispute) to read as a new recital naming the parties to the dispute at the Republic Aviation Corporation facility in Farmingdale, New York, and a cafeteria concessionaire there. It contains no command of its own beyond that rewriting and no date or condition of its own. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11026 Amending Executive Order No. 11025 creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. Because the order only rewrites the text of EO 11025, it has no performance date, report deadline or sunset of its own; the amendment was effective when made and the rewritten text then formed part of EO 11025. EO 11025 is also listed in EO 12553 (its row reads "11025 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the aircraft industry"). A later order, EO 11029 of 1962-06-13, again amended EO 11025, changing its title and substituting new text for its first and second paragraphs. I read the complete held Federal Register copy of EO 11029 (27 FR 5699): it names Executive Order No. 11025 and does not name EO 11026. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments, an order that does not name the target does not end it, and under the strike-and-insert ruling of the same date an amendment is a later event rather than an end. The 1962-06-13 rewording of the same first paragraph is therefore disclosed here as an earlier candidate, not claimed as the end; its source is the held text of EO 11029, which is not one of the cited sources of this claim. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit for this order), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).
